q1.title: Cycle-3 opening rulings
q1.imperative: Record the human's D1-D5 responses. Record as finding.
q1.finding: D1: own-resolution extractor + SCIP test oracle RULED ('agree with your method... definitely like your lighter footprint'). D2: grammar 4+1 accepted as trial vocabulary ('good starting vocabulary'); map-model amendment sign-off still pending. D3: storage DIT — 'run it'. x10.title: Excursion: storage design-it-twice — identity + file layout, three candidates
x10.imperative: Design-it-twice (design-phase form): 3 parallel agents design the statement store's on-disk shape under distinct constraints (diff-ergonomics-first / rename-survival-first / minimal-machinery-first); compared on depth, locality, seam placement, testability + rename scenario, diff-review scenario, tag-attachment scenario, docent-rendering feasibility. Brief: excursions/x10-brief.md. Candidates land at excursions/x10-candidate-{1,2,3}.md; orchestrator synthesis + comparison at excursions/x10-result.md; recommendation presented to the human, who picks. Record the outcome as finding.
x10.finding: Three candidates delivered, genuinely distinct; synthesis at excursions/x10-result.md. UNANIMOUS across all three (probably right): positions out of git (churn poison, measured), facts-not-occurrences, near-zero-diff file moves, no stored edge vocabulary. THE REAL FORK: what deserves identity machinery — C2 protects everything (2-line rename diffs, rename-surviving permalinks; cost: store dead without its ledger, non-auditable diffs, silent-fusion risk, cadence dependence); C3 protects only authored content ([stable-id] = free author-supplied allocator; structural ids disposable because regeneration is 2.3s and the interpreter already forced rename propagation); C1 = C3's identity stance + spends the JSON-lines verdict for skimmable text. RECOMMENDATION: C3 base + commit C2's RUN.md report + build C3's own named guards first (empty-diff assertion, mis-pairing guard, C++ colon fix); C2 machinery and C1 format recorded as untaken roads. C3 lands the tombstone ruling and x9 confidence rule for free. Human's pick pending

x11.title: Excursion: the articles trial — generate real rendered node articles and put them in front of the human
x11.imperative: One named question: do articles generated from the statement store read as a usable alternative to reading the code? Generate rendered articles for all of src/utils from the x7 statement artifacts; deliver the pages to the human; record generation gaps. Brief: excursions/x11-brief.md; result: excursions/x11-result.md. Record the scoped verdict as finding — the human's read of the pages is the real verdict.
x11.finding: Pages generated: 9 modules + index, 3331 lines, pure templating (no model prose; provenance marked per line: 249 lines needed source-fetch [s], 73 from x7a). Entity set exactly complete (87/87, no phantoms). MEASURED VOCABULARY GAPS, ranked: G7 constant values/annotations missing (fatal for constants.py — renders as bare name list); G1 entity kind (method/property/staticmethod) missing; G2 full signatures missing (param NAMES only); G4 docstring body beyond first line discarded (56% of documented entities have bodies); G5 entity spans; G3 decorators (low count, high consequence: @dataclass(frozen=True)); G9 no extraction-window statement (unused vs outside-window ambiguous); G10 stdlib-vs-third-party judged at render time not stored. DEFECT D1: x7b q.line is 0-based, x7a 1-based, schema silent — every source link off by one until renderer corrected. Near-miss finding: dataclass field annotations ARE in the store as unattributed type-reads — vocabulary cannot express the binding. Human's read of the pages = the real verdict, pending. Full: excursions/x11-result.md

q2-articles-ruling.title: Human ruling: article pages go function-by-function
q2-articles-ruling.imperative: Record the human's read of the x11 pages and apply it to the renderer.
q2-articles-ruling.finding: HUMAN RULING 2026-08-07: per-module pages are too long; the map renders one page per entity ('i think we want to do this function by function'). Matches the standing bite-sized-nodes requirement. APPLIED: evidence/x11/render_fn.py reuses render.py's entity_section verbatim, changes only pagination -> articles-fn/: 97 pages (top index + 9 module indexes + 87 entity pages), median entity page 36 lines, max 68 (vs 340+ per-module). Module index keeps doc/deps/constants/linked contents; breadcrumbs map-index / module / parent-class on every page. Skeleton-usefulness verdict still open pending his read of the new granularity.

q3-agent-lean.title: Human ruling: rendered pages are agent-first; aggressively minimize
q3-agent-lean.imperative: Record and apply the agent-first minimization ruling on rendered pages.
q3-agent-lean.finding: HUMAN RULING 2026-08-07: rendered pages are for AGENTS first (human browsing secondary); 'aggressively minimize every excess character'; template text must be renderable ASCII. APPLIED in render_fn.py rewrite: dropped provenance markers, footers, stats/totals lines, breadcrumbs, blockquote prefixes, tables (plain lines), 'generated by' text; entity id is the page title; docstrings stay verbatim (code is truth) including their own 15 non-ASCII lines across 8 pages. Result: median entity page 16 lines (was 36 decorated / 340+ per-module); Config.load_config.md = 964 bytes. Renderer self-checks ASCII on every run and reports residue.

q4-id-syntax.title: Human ruling: on-demand ids; establish anchor syntax + id lookup now
q4-id-syntax.imperative: Record the on-demand-id ruling and put a concrete anchor syntax and id-to-path lookup design on the table.
q4-id-syntax.finding: HUMAN RULING 2026-08-07: minimal storage accepted for the mindmap interface; most functions never need ids; ids minted AS NEEDED when the mindmap hooks a function; syntax must be established NOW for traceability. PROPOSAL ON TABLE (agent): (1) anchor comment = a comment line containing only the bracket token, directly above the def/class/assignment it names, same indent -- works for callables AND constants; slug shares the ruled [kebab-slug] token from the grammar; (2) crawler binds slug to the enclosing entity's symbol path; (3) every regen emits ids.jsonl at the map root, one sorted statement-shaped line per id {id, s, q:{file,line}} -- the single well-known place to resolve an id; deterministic, so its diff IS the id-motion report; (4) mindmap stores repo+slug only, never paths; (5) duplicate slug = build error in run report; deleted slug = the already-ruled orphan gate. Not yet implemented: f1Brainz is read-only this cycle; first real anchors can be written by the dev agent during the cycle-4 real-issue trial.

q5-rulings.title: Rulings: map-model amendment signed off; commenting is a skills function; regen in cycle 4; skills design opens
q5-rulings.imperative: Record the four rulings and open the consumption-skill design discussion.
q5-rulings.finding: HUMAN RULINGS 2026-08-07: (1) map-model.md amendment SIGNED OFF and applied -- explained-by target widened to decision|claim (grammar line 109 + semantics bullet 119), resolving the x9-found contradiction with the doc's own claim-routing prose. (2) Comment-writing adoption is NOT a culture gamble: 'the commenting is a function of our skills' -- agents write tagged comments because the skills direct it; kills the open adoption unknown as a skills-layer design task. (3) Regen/maintenance-loop test folded into the cycle-4 real-issue trial, agreed. (4) 'let's talk skills so we unlock cycle 4' -- consumption+maintenance skill design is the gating work item; discussion opened this turn.

x12.title: Excursion: prior art — giving coding agents maps
x12.imperative: Research excursion: artifact taxonomy, measured usefulness evidence, granularity/token-budget findings, push-vs-pull uptake, freshness, delta to our design. Brief: excursions/x12-brief.md; result: excursions/x12-result.md. Human-commissioned to inform the consumption-skill design gating cycle 4.
x12.finding: Prior art on agent maps: answered with one real contradiction. CONFIRMED (measured): per-entity-and-finer granularity is the field's trend (RepoGraph line-level +8.6-100pct rel on SWE-bench-Lite across 4 frameworks; ARISE statement-level +58pct rel line recall; LocAgent function-level, TraverseGraph ablation isolates the graph); small units beat dumps (1-hop flattened 29.67pct beat 2-hop flattened 26.00pct -- context explosion measured); machine-derived beats hand-written prose (LLM-written AGENTS.md files measured HARMFUL: -0.5 to -2pct success, +20-23pct cost, ETH 2602.11988); ids.jsonl matches LocAgent's name-to-node index; pull-taught-by-loaded-skill matches field answer (ToolFailBench names our #298 zero-invocation as Tool-Skip, best models 86pct clean tool use). Our 5-10 pages x ~200 tokens converges with aider's 1k budget and RepoGraph's optimal ~2.3k 1-hop window. CONTRADICTED: 'overview helps orientation' -- ETH: context files do not provide effective overviews; our #298 orientation-unmoved agrees; two independent lines say maps change WHAT agents read, not how they orient. ESCAPE HATCH = design constraint: generated context helps exactly when NOT cheaply recoverable from source (docs-removed arm: +2.7pct, beats developer-written) -- pages must lead with cross-file structure (referenced-by, blast radius, tombstones), never restate what grep+one-read gives. NUANCE on pull: RepoGraph's deterministic push-into-workflow variants beat agent-invoked-tool variants -- a fixed insertion step is a live alternative arm. GUARD: Codebase-Memory was 10x cheaper but 83pct vs 92pct quality -- hold answer quality first-class in any cycle-4 measurement. PRIZE SIZE: perfect edit-location oracle = +39pp (ORACLE-SWE) -- and repro tests outrank every map. Unconsidered shapes: def-use dataflow edges, runtime call edges. llms.txt: do not borrow (no measured effect). Full: excursions/x12-result.md

q6-handoff-tiers.title: Human ruling: push-then-pull ratified; two-tier handoff (subagents get files, top-level gets index)
q6-handoff-tiers.imperative: Record the push-then-pull ratification and the two-tier handoff pattern; deepen the ETH context-file reading.
q6-handoff-tiers.finding: HUMAN RULINGS 2026-08-07: (1) push-then-pull RATIFIED ('totally agree... this is what we found in our earlier testing'). (2) TWO-TIER HANDOFF: subagent dispatch carries specific 'start with this file here' (deterministic push of the issue's named entity pages); top-level agents get 'look at this INDEX.md to start your exploration' (pointer push, pull from there). (3) Information-fullness required of any provided map. DEEPENED ETH READING (paper fetched, method verified first-hand): the failed LLM-generated context files were NOT slop -- produced by each agent's own vendor-recommended init command+model (Claude Code /init w/ Sonnet-4.5, Codex w/ GPT-5.2, Qwen Code) which DOES explore the repo; dev files avg 641 words/9.7 sections. Slop hypothesis explicitly ablated away: stronger generator models do not help (swap ablation +2pct SWE-bench/-3pct CTXBench), prompt choice no consistent effect, LENGTH no significant impact, removing content categories no change. Instructions ARE followed (uv 1.6x/instance when mentioned vs 0.01 when not) at +10-22pct reasoning tokens -- following costs, overviews just don't navigate: steps-to-first-patched-file unmoved even for DEVELOPER-written overviews. Paper's own conclusion: context files 'should only contain specific additional instructions beyond what is already available in the codebase' = our information-fullness rule verbatim. Quadrant distinction for our design: their failure = push+prose+repo-level-always; ours = targeted-push+derived-facts+entity-level-at-need. Their Python caveat noted (parametric knowledge may nullify context files; niche languages untested).

q7-skills-work.title: Human directive: three skills work items to unlock cycle 4
q7-skills-work.imperative: Execute: (1) update today's map entrance references; (2) subagent instruction generation must hand the specific map entry point for the subagent's work; (3) light role-specific map-use instructions (orchestrator vs implementer: blast radius, tombstones, holes).
q7-skills-work.finding: Three directed items EXECUTED as live skill edits (worktree branch, 4 files): (1) ENTRANCE REFERENCES: scout SKILL.md now enters at the index and pulls only touched packets ('the index is a routing surface, not reading material'); charter AGENT_GUIDE already carried the correct index entry point, untouched. (2) SUBAGENT INSTRUCTION GENERATION: IMPLEMENTER_HANDOFF.template.md Map Anchors gains a 'Map entry point' line (commander names the specific starting file(s); crew never re-derives); commander-core.md anchor-inheritance paragraph now carries the relay rule. (3) ROLE-SPECIFIC USE INSTRUCTIONS: commander-core.md gains orchestrator block (blast radius for gate/wave fencing, recorded failures surfaced in handoffs, holes = cheap adjacent work, push entry points never overview prose); implementer SKILL.md gains use-the-map-before-source paragraph (entry point then referenced-by = blast radius before first edit; map for cross-file questions, source for within-file; tombstone check; missing entry point = Workflow Feedback item not licence to skip). Phrased map-agnostic so today's packet map and the derived map both satisfy the words. Suite: 1378 tests, all 15 fails/errors environmental (missing pytest module in runtime; mutation-floor baseline itself red), zero from these edits.

consolidation.summary: Cycle 3 (refine): storage design-it-twice ran (3 candidates; minimal design accepted with on-demand ids + ids.jsonl lookup; serial-number machinery = named fallback); articles trial ran and drew three granularity/register rulings (one page per entity; agent-first aggressive minimization; ASCII templates); grammar v0 + map-model amendment signed off and applied; x12 prior-art excursion confirmed per-entity pull granularity, refuted the orientation claim, yielded the redundancy rule and push-then-pull ratification; two-tier handoff ruled; three skills work items executed live (entry points in handoffs, entrance references, role-specific use guidance). Cycle 4 = the real-issue dogfood trial: full f1Brainz extraction, one unblocked issue, dev agent with map handoff, regen as part of the trial.
